articleText:
[Hacker News — kadoa.com]
The recent AI sell-off brought a lot of fearmongering headlines. Put next to past stock market crashes, it's only a mild correction for the S&P 500, 6 % below its record. Tech fell harder, with the Nasdaq down 11 % and chip stocks down 36 % , as much as they fell during Covid (35%) . We'll be tracking the sell-off here with daily data updates.

Each line runs from a record high to the low that followed. Eight of the 16 falls past 15% since 1928 are shown.

How far each index is below its record now, against the lows of its own best-known past falls. US chip stocks (the PHLX Semiconductor index) are 36% down from their 22 Jun record, as deep as their Covid fall.

Years from each index's record close to its first close back at or above it. Prices only: with dividends reinvested, most recoveries were shorter. These are worst cases, for someone who bought at the record.
reactions: [Hacker News] It’s just a take on the old, “They predicted twelve of the last three crashes.” If you can’t act on predictions they’re not meaningful.

[Hacker News] > There’s no version of the immediate future where this isn’t the case. Pity you qualified your prediction with "immediate"; a simimlar sentiment was around just before the dot-com crash: "There's no version of the future where we won't be able to use all that extra network infra." Turned out, in the immediate future, just post-crash, we actually didn't need t
[Hacker News] 2020 isn’t exactly history in market terms

[Hacker News] Really? I find local models such as Qwen 3.8 and Muse Glimmer to be pretty good. Not Opus or Sol, but.... Close to Sonnet maybe? So if I had to only use the local models from now on, it would not be a huge loss. Granted, I can't work on parallel on multiple tasks locally. But it's still 48 GB of RAM vs 750 GB or what is required for GLM5.3
[Hacker News] If it's so efficient how come we can't seem to build enough houses... or build anything anymore for that matter?

[Hacker News] As someone not in finance, what actually leads to this pattern (of smaller blips followed by faster recovery)? Is this a consequence of central banks knowing more than before? Algorithmic trading? My intuition is that financial markets seem increasing dissociated from any correlation with street level economy or the financials of traded companies?

items.title: The AI sell-off compared to well-known stock market crashes
